financial_health.basis: Stated in F2 and in the 10-Q MD&A (P4).
financial_health.claim: The third-quarter profit is dominated by a swap gain. Q3 2026 income before income tax was 3,188 (table in millions), including a 1,368 gain on interest rate swaps, against income from operations of 2,295. Interest expense, net was (486) for the quarter and (1,419) for nine months.
quotes: This favorable change was primarily due to an increase in the forward interest rate curves during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a decrease during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4); cash flow amounts are from F3.
financial_health.claim: The company has been actively refinancing and prepaying debt in 2026. The 10-Q lists redeeming the 10.000% CP Funding Redeemable Preferred Units with a new Calcasieu Funding TLB Facility, repaying the Calcasieu Pass Construction Term Loan (due August 2026) with new VGCP 2036 Notes, and redeeming the 8.125% VGLNG 2028 Notes with new 2034 and 2036 notes at 6.375% and 6.625%. It also prepaid $1.9 billion of CP2 Holdings EBL Facilities from Plaquemines commissioning cargo proceeds.
quotes: repaying the outstanding balance of the Calcasieu Pass Construction Term Loan, which was due in August 2026, with proceeds from the newly issued VGCP 2036 Notes
prepaying $1.9 billion outstanding under the CP2 Holdings EBL Facilities with net proceeds received from the sale of commissioning cargos generated by the Plaquemines Project

financial_health.basis: Current debt and cash are stated in F1; the facility and the bridge-loan repayment are stated in the earnings release (P6); the ability to cover maturities is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Debt falling due within twelve months is 1,694 (table in millions) per the balance sheet, against 3,420 of cash and cash equivalents. The company also reports additional committed facilities, including a $3.0 billion 364-day revolving credit facility for general corporate purposes. It has repaid $2.8 billion of a $3.0 billion Equity Bridge Loan for CP2 since the start of 2026.
quotes: secured a $3.0 billion 364-day revolving credit facility to be used for general corporate purposes

financial_health.basis: Stated in the company's earnings release (P6); it is management's forward-looking statement, not a result.
financial_health.claim: Management's 2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $10.0 billion to $10.3 billion, raised from $8.7 billion to $9.1 billion, is a non-GAAP outlook that depends on an assumed liquefaction fee for remaining unsold cargos. It indicates the intended scale of cash generation, but is not audited cash flow.
quotes: Increased Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $10.0 - $10.3 billion

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q risk factors (P5); its link to financing needs is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Further financing needs are signalled by the 10-Q's new risk factor on AI Utility and data center development. The risk factor says such projects may need substantial upfront capital and that the company may need additional financing, which may not be available on favorable terms.
quotes: We may need to seek additional financing to support these investments or to preserve liquidity during periods of market volatility, and such financing may not be available on favorable or acceptable terms or at all.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the MD&A (P4) and the earnings release (P6).
growth_thesis.claim: Higher LNG volumes from the Plaquemines Project ramp-up are the main driver of growth: volumes sold rose to 465.8 TBtu in Q3 from 373.0 TBtu a year earlier, and $827 million of the revenue increase came from volume. For this to continue, Plaquemines commissioning must keep progressing and production must keep ramping.
quotes: Production and LNG sales from our second LNG export facility continue to ramp up as construction and commissioning progress.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4) and the earnings release (P6); risks inferred from the 10-K risk factors (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Plaquemines Phase 1 reached COD after quarter-end and began selling under post-COD SPAs, and Phase 2 COD remains on target for mid-2027. Growth from here depends on Phase 1 delivering to its long-term customers and Phase 2 finishing on schedule.
quotes: COD for Plaquemines Phase 2 remains on target for mid-2027.

growth_thesis.claim: Higher net LNG prices contributed to Q3 growth: the weighted average liquefaction fee was $6.76 against $5.38, and higher liquefaction fees added $640 million to revenue. Over nine months the liquefaction fee was lower, $5.66 against $6.23. For pricing to keep helping, realized liquefaction fees must stay high on uncontracted cargos.
quotes: $640 million increase from higher liquefaction fees primarily from LNG produced by our Plaquemines Project, some of which were sold by VG Commodities under LNG Commissioning Sales Agreements; partially offset by

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6); this is the company's own projection.
growth_thesis.claim: Management raised 2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $10.0 billion - $10.3 billion. The guidance assumes a liquefaction fee of $21.00/MMBtu - $22.00/MMBtu on remaining unsold cargos, so it holds only if forward prices are realized and the cargo volumes are delivered.
quotes: We assume a fixed liquefaction fee range of $21.00/MMBtu - $22.00/MMBtu for our remaining unsold cargos in 2026 in support of our guidance, reflecting market forward prices and recently executed cargo sales.

growth_thesis.basis: Contract totals stated in P4; the contract structure and customer concentration risk stated in the 10-K (P1, P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Long-term contracted SPAs underpin growth: post-COD capacity contracted for CP2 rose from 26.0 mtpa to 29.0 mtpa in 2026. For this to translate into cash, projects must reach COD and customers must perform under take-or-pay contracts.
quotes: In 2026, the CP2 Project entered into or increased contracted capacity under three 20-year post-COD SPAs for the delivery of a combined 3.0 mtpa from Phase 2, increasing total post-COD capacity contracted from 26.0 mtpa to 29.0 mtpa.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P6; the cost-change risk is stated in the 10-K (P3 references it).
growth_thesis.claim: The CP2 Project is the next large capacity addition: Phase 2 reached FID with $8.6 billion of additional financing, $9.8 billion of project costs were incurred in the nine months, and first LNG is now targeted for mid-year 2027. Continuation requires construction to stay on schedule and the pending capacity-increase approvals to be granted.
quotes: we are narrowing the timeline for first LNG production to mid-year 2027

growth_thesis.basis: Pending status stated in P4; FID targets in P6; FID conditions in the 10-K risk factors (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Expansion projects are a further growth option: the Plaquemines Expansion (31.0 mtpa) and CP2 Expansion (11.7 mtpa) both depend on regulatory approvals. The CP2 Expansion has also signed a 20-year SPA for 1.0 mtpa. They need FERC and DOE approvals, offtake contracts and FID.
quotes: Our applications with the FERC and DOE proposing a 31.0 mtpa expansion of the Plaquemines Project are pending approval.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures stated in the cash flow statement (F3); the financing-access condition is inferred from the 10-K risk language (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Growth is financed largely by debt: nine-month capital expenditures of 10,742 exceeded net cash from operating activities of 4,743, and debt issuance and credit-facility draws were 15,421 (cash flow table in millions). Continued growth requires continued access to capital markets and lenders on workable terms.
quotes: we completed several transactions that strengthened our capital structure and liquidity profile

growth_thesis.basis: Design intent stated in the 10-K Business section (P1); risks stated in the risk factors (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Excess-capacity sales are a design-based upside driver: facilities are designed to produce LNG above guaranteed nameplate capacity, in some cases by as much as 40%, to be sold under short-, medium- or long-term arrangements. This requires reliable production above nameplate and buyers for the extra volumes.
quotes: Our facilities are designed to produce LNG in excess of their guaranteed nameplate capacity

growth_thesis.basis: Targets stated in the earnings release (P6); risks stated in the 10-Q (P5). The targets are management's own statements.
growth_thesis.claim: A new line of business is the potential AI utility: frame agreements cover up to 16 new 720 MW power islands, with compute capacity targeted from late 2028 and about 5 GW by the end of 2031. This requires customers, capital, regulatory and land-use approvals, and equipment delivery.
quotes: we have limited experience developing or operating data centers

material_events.basis: stated in the cited 10-Q MD&A and repeated in the earnings release
material_events.claim: The first phase of the Plaquemines Project declared commercial operations (COD) and began selling LNG under its post-COD SPAs.
quotes: On October 31, 2026, the first phase of the Plaquemines Project, our second LNG export facility, declared COD and commenced the sale of LNG under its post-COD SPAs with its phase one customers.

material_events.claim: The company raised its full-year 2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA guidance range. This is a non-GAAP measure and the guidance is forward-looking.
quotes: Increased Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $10.0 - $10.3 billion1, up from $8.7 - $9.1 billion

material_events.basis: stated in the earnings release; the declaration date itself is not printed
material_events.claim: The board declared a cash dividend of $0.04 per share on Class A and Class B common stock, payable after the report date.
quotes: declared a cash dividend of $0.04 per share on its Class A common stock and Class B common stock

material_events.claim: The second phase of the CP2 Project reached FID and the company obtained $8.6 billion of additional project financing.
quotes: In March 2026, Phase 2 of the CP2 Project achieved FID and we obtained $8.6 billion of additional project financing to fund its development and construction.

material_events.claim: The D.C. Circuit unanimously denied the petitions challenging FERC's order authorizing the CP2 Project.
quotes: In August 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit unanimously denied petitions challenging FERC’s order authorizing the CP2 Project.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the cash flow statement also shows a redemption line, and the balance sheet shows redeemable stock of subsidiary at zero at September 30, 2026

quotes: redeeming the CP Funding Redeemable Preferred Units, which carried a stated cash distribution rate of 10.000% and included various liquidity restrictions

material_events.basis: stated in the earnings release; the 10-Q MD&A describes the same agreements as a framework for an option

quotes: In October 2026, Venture Global entered into frame agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes Energy Services for up to 16 new, 720 MW power island units and associated power transformer and grid equipment.

material_events.claim: The company executed 2.0 MTPA of new or increased long-term LNG offtake agreements during and following the third quarter.
quotes: Executed 2.0 MTPA of new or increased 20-year LNG offtake agreements during and following the third quarter:

material_events.basis: stated in the earnings release; the date is given only as during the third quarter through the release date

quotes: secured a $3.0 billion 364-day revolving credit facility to be used for general corporate purposes

risks.basis: inferred from F1, F2 and F3 figures; the financing-availability risk is stated in P5
risks.claim: Construction spending and debt carry exceed operating cash flow, so the company depends on continued access to external financing. Nine-month capital expenditures were 10,742 against net cash from operating activities of 4,743, and long-term debt, net stood at 42,918 with a further 1,694 current (all table in millions). Nine-month interest expense, net was 1,419 (table in millions).
quotes: We may need to seek additional financing to support these investments or to preserve liquidity during periods of market volatility, and such financing may not be available on favorable or acceptable terms or at all.

risks.basis: stated in F2 and P4; the volatility reading is inferred from comparison with 2025 figures in P3
risks.claim: Third-quarter net income was inflated by a swap gain, not only by operations. Gain on interest rate swaps was 1,368 in Q3 and 1,507 for nine months (table in millions). It compares with income from operations of 2,295 in Q3 (table in millions). A reversal in forward rate curves would remove the swap gain and could cut reported earnings.
quotes: This favorable change was primarily due to an increase in the forward interest rate curves during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a decrease during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

risks.claim: Raised 2026 EBITDA guidance rests on an assumed fixed liquefaction fee of $21.00/MMBtu - $22.00/MMBtu for the few remaining unsold cargos, far above the $6.46/MMBtu average on contracted cargos. If market forward prices fall, the guidance could be missed or cut. 99% of available cargos are already contracted.
quotes: We assume a fixed liquefaction fee range of $21.00/MMBtu - $22.00/MMBtu for our remaining unsold cargos in 2026 in support of our guidance, reflecting market forward prices and recently executed cargo sales.

risks.basis: stated in P4; the 10-K approval risk is in P1's footnotes
risks.claim: Several capacity increases and expansions depend on pending FERC and DOE approvals. The CP2 increase from 28.0 mtpa to 35.0 mtpa, the Plaquemines increase to 35.0 mtpa and both expansion projects are pending. Delay or denial would limit planned growth.
quotes: Our applications with the FERC and DOE to increase the CP2 Project's permitted production and authorized export capacity from 28.0 mtpa to 35.0 mtpa are pending approval.

risks.basis: stated in P5 and P4; scale of spending is not given
risks.claim: The move into data center and AI-utility power development is outside the core LNG business and may divert capital and management attention. The company says it has limited experience in data centers. It has entered frame agreements for up to 16 new power islands and cites potential of up to 10 GW of compute capacity.
quotes: we have limited experience developing or operating data centers

risks.basis: stated in P2 and P1; concentration figures are as of FY2025
risks.claim: Revenue is concentrated in a few customers. In 2025 about 50.0% of revenue from individual external customers came from three customers, and one customer was approximately 23% of revenue. Failure or termination by a large customer could hit cash flow.
quotes: Moreover, for the year ended December 31, 2025, we had one customer which represented approximately 23% of our revenue for that same period.

risks.basis: inferred from P2's stated risk and P4/P6 figures
risks.claim: As Plaquemines Phase 1 moved to COD, higher-priced commissioning sales give way to contracted SPA pricing. The nine-month weighted average liquefaction fee fell to $5.66 from $6.23, and the 10-K warns that commissioning proceeds may be more valuable than post-COD revenue. Earnings growth then depends on volume and excess-capacity sales.
quotes: If COD occurs earlier than expected for a particular project or phase thereof, it would adversely impact our ability to generate proceeds from the sale of commissioning cargos, which, subject to market conditions, may otherwise be more valuable than the revenues earned under our post-COD SPAs.

risks.basis: stated in P6 forward-looking statements; magnitude unknown

quotes: We may need to seek additional financing to support these investments or to preserve liquidity during periods of market volatility, and such financing may not be available on favorable or acceptable terms or at all.

quotes: Our applications with the FERC and DOE to increase the Plaquemines Project's permitted production and authorized export capacity from 27.2 mtpa to 35.0 mtpa are pending approval.
